notes: Same access route/method as bs25 (direct HTTP, Demandware SSR HTML, no block). Discovery: homepage mega-menu has a dedicated red-highlighted 'Sale' top-nav entry whose flyout explicitly separates two distinct sections: a generic 'Shop All Sale' section (department 'X Sale' pages, e.g. /c/sale/furniture/, /c/sale/kitchen/ - these are the current 'Labor Day Weekend Sale' promo, a temporary markdown campaign, NOT taken as Clearance per the Sale-vs-Clearance test) and a visually distinct 'Clearance' section (text-color-red, bold) linking to /c/sale/clearance/ and per-department 'Clearance X' pages. The site's own on-page copy repeatedly calls this permanent-markdown tier 'Red-Ticket Clearance' (e.g. promo banner 'Extra 50% Off Red-Ticket Clearance Items'), and every Clearance page's own H1/breadcrumb reads 'Clearance' or 'Clearance <Dept>' - a clean, unambiguous site-taxonomy signal distinct from the temporary Sale campaign, so these qualify per brief Section 3. /c/sale/clearance/ and /c/sale/clearance/shop-all-clearance/ returned byte-identical content (same 564-item grid, same H1 'Clearance') - true alias, canonical /c/sale/clearance/ kept, alias dropped. Cross-checked nav against sitemap_8-category.xml: found 2 additional clearance-* department pages not linked in the header nav (Clearance Holidays, Clearance Rugs) - both fetched and included. Two more sitemap entries, /c/sale/clearance/clearance-furniture/ and /c/sale/clearance/clearance-outdoor/, now return HTTP 404 (confirmed via curl) - stale/seasonal sitemap entries, currently empty categories taken down, excluded (not a block). Every qty is the PLP's own SSR 'N Items' grid header. No local-language search needed (US/English site); site search itself (/search*) not queried directly since it's robots-disallowed for all crawlers and nav+sitemap already gave complete, unambiguous coverage.
